level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall

Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

1	# Integration guide: frontend (`web/`) ↔ backend (`backend/`)
2	
3	**For:** whoever (human or AI agent) connects the synthetic-data frontend to Ghassen's real backend.
4	**State as of 11.10.2026, 02:30:** frontend on branch `feature/frontend-demo` ([PR #5](https://github.com/ghassenzaara/BMW-Product-Management-Challenge/pull/5) into `main`); backend on `main` (phases 0 to 10 done, see `plan.md`).
5	
6	> **How to use this file.** Read sections 1 to 3 to understand the product and the two codebases, then section 7 (the gap) and section 8 (the plan). Sections 4 to 6 are reference material: every screen, endpoint and business rule of the frontend, so nothing gets lost while swapping the data source.

9	
10	## 0. TL;DR
11	
12	- The **frontend** is a Next.js 16 app that talks to **its own REST contract** (`web/src/contracts/*.ts`, Zod, exported to `contracts/openapi.yaml`). Today that contract is served by a **mock backend inside Next.js** (`web/src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts` + `web/src/mock/`) on synthetic data plus 404 real BMW verbatims.
13	- The **backend** is FastAPI + Postgres/pgvector (Supabase) with **its own, different REST API** (`backend/app/api/routers/*.py`, guide in `backend/API.md`), on the full real data (1,206 cases, ~13,000 signals, scores for 10 configs, RAG index).
14	- The two APIs **do not match** (different paths, field names, vocabularies, IDs and concepts: per-vehicle case state, configs and weight profiles per vehicle × market, page-based requirements). About half of the UI features (open questions, meeting notes, referrals, innovation pool, vehicle plan, comments, alerts, head sign-off, quality check, segments, deck) **have no backend counterpart yet**.
15	- **Recommended approach: an adapter layer (BFF) inside Next.js.** Keep the UI and its contract unchanged; replace the mock handlers endpoint by endpoint with handlers that call FastAPI and map the shapes. Features the backend lacks keep running on a small "sidecar" store keyed by real IDs. Switchable per endpoint, so the demo can always fall back to the mock. Details and step-by-step plan in section 8.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 1. The product in one page
20	
21	BMW product managers (PMs) decide which customer requirements go into the next generation of a vehicle (G60 = 5 Series, F70 = 1 Series, G70 = 7 Series). The app turns heterogeneous evidence into traceable, prioritized requirements, with the PM deciding at every step.
22	
23	**Chain:** `Signal → Case → Requirement → Vehicle plan → Codebeamer`
24	
25	| Concept | Meaning | Frontend entity | Backend table |
26	|---|---|---|---|
27	| **Signal** | One piece of evidence with its source: a BMW verbatim, a study row, a web review, a competitor fact | `Signal` | `signal` (+ `source_record`) |
28	| **Case** | A customer **problem**, built from a group of signals on one topic. Has an importance score, **no cost** | `Case` | `case_item` + `case_vehicle` (per line) + `case_score` |
29	| **Requirement** | What BMW builds to solve a confirmed case: SMART text, measurable targets, release, rough cost | `Requirement` | `requirement` |
30	| **Vehicle plan** | Requirements of a series grouped by car area, next to today's equipment; exported to Codebeamer | `VehiclePlan` / `PlannedFeature` | (none; `vehicle_feature` holds today's equipment) |
31	
32	**Non-negotiable rules (both codebases agree):**
33	1. **AI proposes, PM decides.** The AI never edits directly: it returns proposals (frontend `Proposal`, backend `chat_message.proposed_diff`) that a person accepts or rejects.
34	2. **Every human decision has a reason** and every change writes an **append-only audit event** (who or what, when, before/after, rationale).
35	3. **Traceability:** every requirement links back to its case, the case to its signals, signals to their source quote.
36	4. **Fixed taxonomy:** 11 car areas, 219 topics, 11 aspect groups (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`). Agents classify into it; they never invent categories (Thomas's feedback).
37	5. **Customer-facing requirements only:** regulatory, engineering specs and pricing are out of scope.
38	6. **Score formula is explainable:** case score = weighted mean of factors (0..1); requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier (S/M/L).

67	## 3. How the frontend works (architecture)
68	
69	### 3.1 Contract-first
70	- Every endpoint is declared once in `web/src/contracts/api.ts` (`endpoints` object: method, path, query, body, response as Zod schemas). Entities in `entities.ts`, vocabularies in `enums.ts`, UI labels in `labels.ts`.
71	- `npm run export-contract` writes `contracts/openapi.yaml` and `contracts/schemas/*.json`.
72	- `npm run contract-test` (`API_BASE=…`) calls every endpoint against a running server, validates every response with Zod, and walks the demo storyline. **Any data source behind the UI must pass it** (the storyline uses seeded IDs such as `CASE-G60-0001`, so it needs parametrizing for real data).
73	
74	### 3.2 Data access
75	- The UI never imports `src/mock`. It calls `api(name, { params, query, body })` from `src/lib/api/client.ts`, or the hooks `useApi(name, opts)` / `useApiMutation(name)` from `src/lib/api/hooks.ts`.
76	- Base URL: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` (default `/api` = the mock route).
77	- **Every successful mutation invalidates every query** (`qc.invalidateQueries()`): simple and always consistent, fine for demo-sized data. With 13,000 real signals some screens will need pagination (section 9).
78	- Errors: the client expects `{ error: string, issues? }` and an HTTP status; it throws `ApiRequestError`, shown as a toast.
79	
80	### 3.3 Auth (demo)
81	- `/login` lists users (`GET /users`); picking one sets the cookie `rs_user` (`src/lib/session.ts`). The client sends it as header `x-user-id`. The mock route resolves the user from its store (`u-lena`, `u-wei`, `u-jonas`, `u-katrin`, `u-sofia`, `u-daniel`).
82	
83	### 3.4 The mock backend
84	- `route.ts` matches method + path against the contract, parses query/body with Zod, calls `handlers[name]({ params, query, body, user })`, validates the response in dev, maps `ApiError(status)` to JSON errors.
85	- `src/mock/store.ts`: one in-memory `Dataset` (shape = `Dataset` entity) cloned from `fixtures/seed.json`; `audit()`, `notify()`, `nextId()`, `now()`; `POST /admin/reset` restores the seed. Quality checks live in a side map (`checks()`).
86	- `src/mock/handlers.ts`: one function per endpoint, holding the business rules (section 6).
87	- `src/mock/scoring.ts`: reference scorer. `src/mock/ai/*`: scripted AI (chat intents, drafts, meeting-note extraction, quality check, segments); `ai/live.ts` optionally calls Claude when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set (free-form chat, quality-check LLM pass, segment summary). The backend uses OpenAI; after integration the chat should go to the backend RAG agent.
88	- Seed: `npm run seed` rebuilds `seed.json` from the real CSVs in `docs/02-data/processed/` (404 selected verbatims, study rows, 2030 sales) plus authored synthetic content (people, web signals, competitor facts, decisions, requirements, audit history). Synthetic objects carry `synthetic: true` and the UI tags them.

220	## 6. Business logic implemented in the frontend mock
221	
222	These rules live in `web/src/mock/handlers.ts` and `web/src/mock/ai/*`. Whatever replaces the mock must keep them (in the backend, the adapter or the sidecar).
223	
224	### 6.1 Permissions
225	- Only the case **owner or a co-owner** (or the head) changes a case; everyone can read, comment, watch, escalate. Only the requirement owner (or head) edits it.
226	- **Head of product line** (`role = head`) sends back, signs off, resolves escalations, edits the brand profile and default weight profiles.
227	- Series PMs (plan `ownerIds`) edit the vehicle plan.
228	
229	### 6.2 Case lifecycle (frontend)
230	- States: `observed → new → investigating → awaiting_answers → ready → decided`. Actions `open`, `start`, `await`, `ready`, `reopen` move the state; every move needs a rationale.
231	- Deciding sets `state = decided` and an **outcome**: `confirm` (drafts requirements via the requirement agent if none exist), `refer` (to another PM: creates a `Referral`, the receiver becomes a watcher and is notified), `innovation` (adds to the pool with a horizon and the PM's pitch), `park`, `reject`, `merge` (moves signals into the target, recomputes its figures, notifies the target owner).
232	- `refer` with `escalate: true` creates an **escalation** to the head instead (anyone involved may escalate, e.g. China vs. rest-of-world conflict).
233	- Every decision is prepended to the case page's "Decision log" and audited.
234	- Referral decisions: `accept` creates a **linked case** in the receiver's workspace (`originCaseId`), `decline` puts the source case back to `ready`, `escalate` hands it to the head, `resolve` (head) records a resolution (one market, market variant, keep both, take over, return) in the case context and decision log.
235	
236	### 6.3 Requirement lifecycle (frontend)
237	`draft → in_discussion → pm_approved → signed_off → planned → exported`, plus `rejected` (restore → `draft`).
238	- `approve` (owner, from draft or in discussion) notifies the head with a sign-off request; the open quality-check issues are recorded in the audit event (section 6.9).
239	- `send_back` (head, from pm_approved) → `in_discussion` with `sentBackReason`, owner notified.
240	- `sign_off` (head, from pm_approved) → owner notified.
241	- `plan` (owner/head, from signed_off) links or creates a `PlannedFeature` in the series plan.
242	- `export` (from planned); the Codebeamer export also moves every planned requirement to `exported`.
243	- IDs: `REQ-<series>-NNNN`, China variants `REQ-<series>-CN-NNNN`.
244	
245	### 6.4 Scoring (reference, `mock/scoring.ts`)
246	- Factors (all 0..1): `customers`, `severity`, `satisfaction_gap`, `competitor_gap`, `market_volume`, `regression`, `trend`, `brand_fit`.
247	- `case score = Σ w_f · factor_f / Σ w_f` (no cost). `requirement score = case score × costMultiplier[size]`.
248	- Manual ranks (with reason) win over the computed order. Observed, rejected and merged cases are not ranked.
249	- `previewScores` re-ranks with unsaved weights; the UI shows "moved because…" and a robustness column (stays in the top 5 under every profile).
250	- `customers` is recomputed from the case's signals: `log10(1 + n) / log10(61)`.
251	
252	### 6.5 AI assistant (`mock/ai/chat.ts`, scripted unless a key is set)
253	Intent by message text; every answer cites evidence as `[SIGNAL-ID]`, and every change is a proposal:
254	- "research …" → mock research run adds two synthetic web signals to the case (audited as `agent:researcher`).
255	- "draft a SMART requirement" → `new_requirement` proposal(s) from `ai/drafts.ts`.
256	- "what should I ask engineering/finance" → `new_question` proposals.
257	- "why is this ranked so high", "compare the markets", "what do competitors offer", "argument sheet", "set the target to …" (field proposal) → cited answers.
258	- Free-form questions go to the live LLM when available (context: case, figures, up to 40 signals, page, requirement).
259	- `savePmContext` stores the PM's market focus, cost sensitivity, positioning, timing and note in the case context, then the assistant posts 1 to 2 follow-up questions the data cannot answer (market mismatch, platform change vs. LCI, paid option vs. standard, match/beat competitors).
260	- `addMeetingNote` (`ai/notes.ts`) extracts answers to open questions, field updates and decision-log entries from pasted notes as proposals.
261	- Proposal kinds: `field`, `body`, `question_answer`, `new_question`, `new_requirement`. Accepting applies the change, logs a context entry and an audit event.
262	
263	### 6.6 Monitoring and refresh
264	- `refresh` runs once over a pool of authored web findings: new signals attach to their case, owners and watchers are notified, a competitor fact with a metric raises an **alert** ("raises the bar") on the case; a second run finds nothing (dedupe by URL and content hash). An `AgentRun` is recorded.
265	- `resolveAlert`: dismiss, or `rework` (requirement back to in_discussion, case back to investigating).
266	
267	### 6.7 Vehicle plan and export
268	- The plan lists features per car area with today's availability (standard/optional/absent/removed), action (keep/new/improve/remove), release, protected flag and linked requirements.
269	- Codebeamer CSV columns: ID, Summary, Description, Category, Market, Release, Priority, Score, Evidence level, Metrics, Acceptance criteria, Assumptions, Cost size, Cost band, Linked case, Linked findings, Rationale, Status. Sorted by rank under the user's weight profile.
270	
271	### 6.8 Engineering deck (`requirementDeck` + `web/src/lib/deck.ts`)
272	Signed-off, planned and exported requirements of a series, sorted by rank. Per slide: SMART text and metrics, top 3 BMW complaint quotes (not likes), score breakdown (factor value × normalized weight), competitor gap, last 5 decisions (requirement and case), open quality issues. Rendered client-side with `pptxgenjs`. Easy to rebuild on real data: it only needs requirement, case factors + weights, case signals and decisions.
273	
274	### 6.9 Quality check (`mock/ai/quality.ts`)
275	Runs automatically after drafting and every edit, and on demand. Warns, never blocks; approving lists the open issues and requires a reason.
276	- `vague_word` (title, description, acceptance criteria: "improved", "better", "user-friendly", "intuitive", "seamless", …; red if no metric has a numeric target).
277	- `missing_scope` (scope global while > 80 % of the case's verbatims come from one market; China scope with < 3 Chinese verbatims).
278	- `out_of_scope` (homologation, type approval, UN-R, ISO 26262, emissions, crash test, ECU, CAN bus, supplier, part number, price/pricing, business case) — red.
279	- `duplicate` (≥ 30 % word overlap with a live requirement of the same series, red) / `baukasten` (same in another series, or the case spans several series, amber, suggests the cross-series PM).
280	- `conflict` (same metric question with another target in the same car area; or relies on a feature the plan removes).
281	- Optional LLM pass adds issues of the same kinds (strict JSON, related IDs validated).
282	Portable as-is: inputs are a requirement, its case figures, all requirements and the plan. Could later move to Python next to `requirements/service.py`.
283	
284	### 6.10 Ask the segment (`mock/ai/segment.ts`)
285	- Segments = markets of the case (+ market × powertrain with ≥ 3 verbatims), counted **only from real BMW verbatims** (no synthetic, no web).
286	- With verbatims: counts by kind + 3 to 5 strongest quotes, cited. Live LLM gets only that segment's quotes and must summarize in the third person; citations not in the set are dropped.
287	- Without verbatims: "No evidence for China owners", the closest segment with data, and a `new_question` proposal to the market PM. Never a guess.
288	- On real data: segments come from `GET /signals?case_id=…` filtered by `evidence_role = bmw_customer` (or `source_id = bmw_feedback`), grouped by `market` and `powertrain`.
289	
290	### 6.11 Audit actions written by the mock
291	`case.created/edited/state_changed/decided/pm_context_saved/exported_md`, `requirement.drafted/edited/status_changed/checked/deck_exported`, `requirements.exported`, `proposal.accepted/rejected/created`, `question.created/answered/edited`, `meeting_note.added`, `referral.*`, `escalation.*`, `alert.*`, `plan.feature_*`, `signals.fetched/researched`, `segment.asked`, `comment.added`, `weight_profile.*`, `brand_profile.updated`, `workspace.updated`. Actor = user id or `agent:<name>`.
292	
293	---
294	
295	## 7. The backend on `main` (what exists)
296	
297	**Stack:** Python 3.12, FastAPI, psycopg, Supabase Postgres + pgvector (local embedded Postgres for dev), OpenAI (chat + embeddings; key still missing → offline fallbacks), `uv`.
298	
299	**Run:**
300	```bash
301	cd backend
302	cp .env.example .env          # Supabase URL/keys or leave empty for local; AUTH_MODE=dev for X-User-Id
303	uv run python -m app.demo build --fresh   # local DB: migrate, seed, cases, scores, RAG, demo users (~10 min)
304	uv run python -m app.demo users           # prints demo user ids
305	uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload      # http://localhost:8000/docs
306	```
307	CORS already allows `http://localhost:3000`.
308	
309	**Auth:** `AUTH_MODE=dev` → header `X-User-Id: <app_user uuid>`; production → `Authorization: Bearer <Supabase JWT>`. Demo users (fixed ids):
310	`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001` Demo PM 5 Series (`pm`, `[G60]`), `…0002` PM 7 Series (`[G70]`), `…0003` PM 1 Series (`[F70]`), `…0004` engineer, `…0005` admin. Roles: `pm`, `engineer`, `admin`; a PM acts only on the lines in `app_user.vehicles` (empty = all).
311	
312	**Core concepts that differ from the frontend:**
313	- **Config** = one PM view: vehicle × market (`G60 / USA`). Each config has several **weight profiles**; scores and ranks exist **per profile**. Boards always need `profile_id`.
314	- **Case is not tied to one vehicle**: `case_item` (topic + aspect group, page `body_md` with `body_version`, figures per vehicle × market × powertrain, brand fit, segment) and `case_vehicle` (per line: state `observed | open | confirmed | rejected`, opened-by rule, market conflict, release fit, manual rank, new-evidence flag). Case IDs `CASE-0012`.
315	- **Requirement** is a page: `title`, `body_md` (+ version, stale saves → 409), `metric_target` (jsonb), `acceptance_criteria`, `assumptions`, `release_target` (`next_gen | current_car | ota`), `evidence_level` (`bmw_data | web | assumption`), `cost_size` + `cost_source`, status `draft | in_discussion | approved | rejected | deleted` (tombstone). IDs `REQ-G60-0012` (number = case number), `REQ-G60-USA-0012` when split per market. Generated when the PM confirms the case for a line.
316	- **Scoring:** factors `distinct_customers, severity, satisfaction_gap, competitor_gap, market_volume, removed_vs_predecessor, reach, trend`; `score = brand_multiplier × Σ w·f / Σ w` (brand fit is a **multiplier** `fits 1.0 / neutral 0.8 / off_brand 0.5`, not a factor); requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier (`S 1.0, M 0.85, L 0.7`; missing cost = 1.0). Manual ranks first; `score_moved` flag when a score changes by ≥ 0.1.
317	- **RAG sidebar agent:** hybrid search (full text + pgvector), tools `search_signals, get_case, get_requirement, score_breakdown, compare_markets, what_if_weights, propose_edit`; citations `[signal:<uuid>]` must have been retrieved, else "No evidence found in the stored sources."; edits are a proposed page diff accepted via `/chat/messages/{id}/decision`.
318	- **Signals:** uuid ids, `record_id` → `source_record` (exact quote checkable), `evidence_role` (`bmw_customer | competitor | market`), `kind`, `severity`, topic (`feature`), `aspect_group`, `car_area[]`, `market` (`USA | China | Europe | Rest of World | unknown`), `powertrain`, `scope_tag`, `validation` (`valid | quarantined | deleted`).
319	- **Audit:** `audit_event` append-only (`actor` like `pm:<uuid>`, `agent:rag`, `seed:…`), `decision` table for PM actions, `page_version` for page history, `log_access` for views and exports.
320	
321	**Endpoints (about 50):** see the table in `backend/API.md`. Highlights the UI does not use yet: case page versions and stale-save protection, merge/split, tag overrides (brand fit, segment, release fit), predecessor research, profile compare (robust top N), config source filter, quarantine release/delete, taxonomy review queue, audit chain report per requirement, overview map per line, signal detail with its source record.
322	
323	---
324	
325	## 8. The gap and the recommended plan
326	
327	### 8.1 Vocabulary mapping (adapter must translate both ways)
328	
329	| Concept | Frontend | Backend |
330	|---|---|---|
331	| Market | `EU`, `US`, `CN`, `RoW`, `unknown` | `Europe`, `USA`, `China`, `Rest of World`, `unknown` |
332	| Requirement scope | `marketScope`: `global` \| `RoW` \| `CN` | `market`: null (all) or one market when split |
333	| User role | `vehicle_pm`, `attribute_pm`, `head` | `pm` (lines in `vehicles`), `engineer`, `admin` |
334	| User id | `u-lena` … | uuid (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000X`) |
335	| Case id | `CASE-G60-0001` | `CASE-0012` (opaque string either way; UI only displays it) |
336	| Case series | `series` + `relatedSeries` | `case_vehicle` rows (series = the current config's vehicle, related = the others) |
337	| Case state | `observed, new, investigating, awaiting_answers, ready, decided` + outcome | per vehicle `observed, open, confirmed, rejected` (+ `case_lineage` for merges) |
338	| Requirement status | `draft, in_discussion, pm_approved, signed_off, planned, exported, rejected` | `draft, in_discussion, approved, rejected, deleted` |
339	| Release | `next_gen`, `lci`, `ota` | `next_gen`, `current_car`, `ota` |
340	| Evidence level | `high, medium, low, assumption` | `bmw_data, web, assumption` |
341	| Score factors | `customers, severity, satisfaction_gap, competitor_gap, market_volume, regression, trend, brand_fit` | `distinct_customers, severity, satisfaction_gap, competitor_gap, market_volume, removed_vs_predecessor, reach, trend` + brand **multiplier** |
342	| Cost source | `option_price, ai_estimate, pm, finance` | `option_price, ai_estimate, pm, engineering` |
343	| Weight profile | per user workspace, global | per config (vehicle × market) |
344	| Brand profile | `pillars[]`, `doNot[]`, `notesMd` | versioned `body_md` |
345	| Citations in chat | `[G60-1430]`, `[SIG-…]` (UI links them) | `[signal:<uuid>]` |
346	| Proposals | own entity, 5 kinds | `chat_message.proposed_diff` (page body diff) only |
347	| Signal source | `agent` + `sourceType` + `trust` | `evidence_role` + `source_record.source_id` / `content_type` / `category` |
348	| Taxonomy payload | `{version, carAreas[{id,label,description}], topics[{id,label,shortLabel,carArea,hint}], aspectGroups[{id,description}]}` | `{car_areas[{code,name,description}], aspect_groups[{code,description}], topics[{id(uuid),topic_id,name,car_area,hint}]}` |
349	
350	### 8.2 Feature coverage
351	
352	| Area | Backend has it | Missing on the backend (needs sidecar or a backend extension) |
353	|---|---|---|
354	| Signals, quarantine, taxonomy, runs | yes | trigger a fetch run from the UI (`refresh`), `trust` tier, `agent` label |
355	| Case board, page, scores | yes (per profile) | owner / co-owners / watchers, the finer workflow states (investigating, awaiting answers, ready), outcomes refer / innovation / park, `highlights`, PM context, create a case from loose signals, what-if preview endpoint |
356	| Requirements | yes (page-based) | structured SMART fields edit (`metrics[]` with basis/benchmark, acceptance criteria, assumptions, marketScope) as an endpoint; head sign-off, plan and export statuses; send back reason; owner |
357	| Chat | yes (RAG, cited, page diffs) | proposals other than page diffs (new question, new requirement, field), research runs, PM-context follow-ups, segment mode |
358	| Collaboration | notifications, decisions, audit per object | users list, open questions, meeting notes, referrals and escalations, innovation pool, comments + mentions, alerts with resolve, global audit list, search |
359	| Vehicle plan | today's equipment in `vehicle_feature` | plan features (action, protected, release), plan endpoints, Codebeamer CSV in the UI's column set, deck payload |
360	| Quality check, segments | — | both (frontend logic is portable, section 6.9 / 6.10) |
361	
362	### 8.3 Options
363	
364	1. **Adapter / BFF in Next.js (recommended).** Keep the UI and its contract. Add backend-backed handlers next to the mock handlers, same `Handlers` type, choose per endpoint. UI-only collaboration objects live in a sidecar store keyed by real backend IDs. Pros: zero UI churn, contract test still guards the shapes, instant fallback to the mock for the demo, backend unchanged. Cons: mapping code; sidecar is in-memory until persisted.
365	2. **Implement the frontend contract in FastAPI** (a new `ui` router that serves `contracts/openapi.yaml`, plus tables for the missing features). Cleanest long-term, everything audited in Postgres; more Python work and riskier before a demo.
366	3. **Rewrite the UI against `backend/API.md`.** Most churn; loses features the backend lacks.
367	
368	A good path: start with option 1 now, and move pieces into the backend (option 2) when they stabilize (users list, statuses, structured requirement patch, questions, referrals).
369	
370	### 8.4 Step-by-step plan (option 1)
371	
372	**Step 0 — Branch and run both.**
373	- Merge PR #5 (or merge `main` into `feature/frontend-demo` again: `main` gained phases 7 to 10 after the PR was opened). Work on a new branch `feature/integration`.
374	- Run the backend locally (`AUTH_MODE=dev`, `python -m app.demo build --fresh`, uvicorn on :8000) and the web app (:3000).
375	
376	**Step 1 — Plumbing.**
377	- `web/.env.local`: `DATA_SOURCE=backend`, `BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8000`.
378	- New folder `web/src/backend/`:
379	  - `client.ts`: server-side `fetch` to `BACKEND_URL` with `X-User-Id` (or Bearer), JSON errors → `ApiError(status, detail)` (FastAPI errors are `{detail}`).
380	  - `map.ts`: all vocabulary mappings of 8.1, in both directions, unit-tested.
381	  - `handlers.ts`: `Partial<Handlers>` implemented against the backend.
382	  - `sidecar.ts`: in-memory store for UI-only objects (questions, meeting notes, PM context, referrals, innovation, plan features, comments, alerts, proposals of non-diff kinds, owner/workflow state, quality checks), keyed by backend IDs; reuse `mock/store.ts` helpers.
383	- `route.ts`: pick `backendHandlers[name] ?? mockHandlers[name]` when `DATA_SOURCE=backend`; keep the mock as the default.
384	- **Users and personas:** keep the persona UX. Map personas to backend users with a table in the adapter (e.g. Lena → `…0001` PM 5 Series; Daniel → `…0002`; Sofia → `…0003`; Katrin → `…0005` admin acting as head; Jonas → a PM with all lines; Wei → a second 5 Series PM, needs a new `app_user` row). `users` returns the persona list with backend ids attached.
385	- **Config choice:** each persona needs a config (vehicle × market) and default weight profile from `GET /configs`. Proposal: Lena → `G60 / USA` (most G60 verbatims are US), Wei → `G60 / China`, Sofia → `F70 / Europe`, Daniel → `G70 / USA`; `updateWorkspace` switches config/profile. `me.workspace.weightProfileId` = that profile id.
386	
387	**Step 2 — Read path (what the screens show).**
388	- `taxonomy`, `quarantine`, `agentRuns`, `notifications` (+ `readNotifications` by looping ids): pure mapping.
389	- `cases`: `GET /cases?profile_id=<workspace profile>&state=observed&state=open&state=confirmed&state=rejected` → map each board row to a full `Case` (fill fields the board lacks with defaults or a per-case `GET /cases/{id}` when needed; owner from sidecar, default = the persona of the config). `figures.perMarket` from `markets` (customers, negative share).
390	- `caseBundle`: `GET /cases/{id}` + `GET /signals?case_id=…&limit=500` (+ sidecar questions, referrals, alerts, notes, proposals). Map `figures.by_vehicle[vehicle]` to `figures.perMarket`, `scores[]` of the current profile to `factors`, `decisions` + `body_md` to the page.
391	- `signals`: `GET /signals` with mapped filters; map `id` (uuid), `market`, `kind`, `severity`, `quote`/`quote_en`, topic, aspect group, car area, `source_id`/`content_type` → `sourceType`/`agent`, `evidence_role = bmw_customer` → `agent = bmw_data`, `synthetic = false`. Pagination: the Sankey needs aggregates, not 13,000 rows (see section 9).
392	- `requirements` / `requirementBundle`: `GET /requirements?profile_id=…&status=…` and `GET /requirements/{id}`; map `metric_target`, `acceptance_criteria`, `assumptions`, `release_target`, `evidence_level`, `cost_*`, `market` → `marketScope`; the sidecar adds the signed-off / planned / exported layer, owner and quality check.
393	- `scores`: build `ScoresResponse` from the board rows (score, rank) and the per-profile factor breakdown of `GET /cases/{id}` (`scores[].factors[f].contribution`), or add a backend endpoint returning factors on the board.
394	- `weightProfiles`: profiles of the persona's config (`GET /configs`), factor names mapped; `brand_fit` slider ↔ brand multipliers (decision needed, 8.5).
395	- `audit`: per object → `GET /audit/{object_type}/{object_id}` (map `actor` `pm:<uuid>` → persona id); global list → needs a backend endpoint (or merge per-object calls for the current case and requirements).
396	- `brandProfile`: backend `body_md` → `notesMd`; pillars from the sidecar or parsed headings.
397	
398	**Step 3 — Write path.**
399	- `transitionCase`: `confirm | reject | reopen | open` → `POST /cases/{id}/vehicles/{vehicle}/transition` (vehicle = the persona's line); `merge` → `POST /cases/{id}/merge {target_id, rationale}` (backend refuses cross-topic merges); `start | await | ready | refer | innovation | park` and escalations → sidecar (backend state stays `open`). After confirm, the backend returns the generated requirement ids.
400	- `generateRequirements` → `POST /cases/{id}/vehicles/{vehicle}/requirements`.
401	- `patchCase`: `bodyMd`/`title` → `PUT /cases/{id}/page` with `expected_version = bodyVersion` (409 → toast "someone saved first, reload"); `brandFit` → `POST /cases/{id}/tags {field: "brand_fit", …}` (map 0..1 → fits/neutral/off_brand); `manualRank` → `POST …/vehicles/{v}/rank`; watchers / co-owners → sidecar.
402	- `transitionRequirement`: `discuss` → status `in_discussion`, `approve` → `approved`, `reject` → `rejected`, `restore` → `draft`; `send_back | sign_off | plan | export` → sidecar layer on top of backend `approved` (or extend the backend status flow, 8.5).
403	- `patchRequirement`: `releaseTarget` → `/retarget`, `cost.size` → `/cost`, `manualRank` → `/rank`, everything else (title, description, metrics, acceptance criteria, assumptions, scope) → render into `body_md` and `PUT /page` with the version, or add a structured PATCH on the backend (preferred, 8.5).
404	- `postMessage` (no segment) → `POST /chat/{type}/{id} {question}`; map the agent row to `ChatMessage` (rewrite `[signal:<uuid>]` to `[<uuid>]` and fill `citations` from `cited_signals`); a `proposed_diff` becomes a `Proposal { kind: "body", id: <message id> }`. `decideProposal` on such an id → `POST /chat/messages/{id}/decision {accept}`; other proposal kinds stay in the sidecar/scripted flow.
405	- `postMessage` with `segment` and `caseSegments`: compute in the adapter from the case's real signals (port of `mock/ai/segment.ts`).
406	- `exportRequirements`: map to `GET /requirements/export?profile_id=…&format=csv` or build the UI's Codebeamer CSV from the requirements (the backend export is "approved top N" only; it logs the export in `decision` and `audit_event` either way).
407	- Weight profiles: `createWeightProfile` → `POST /configs/{id}/profiles`, `saveWeightProfile` → `PATCH /profiles/{id}`; `previewScores` → recompute in the adapter from stored factor values (`score = brand × Σ w·f / Σ w`) or add a backend preview endpoint.
408	
409	**Step 4 — UI-only features on real data (sidecar).**
410	Open questions, meeting notes (+ `ai/notes.ts`), PM context (+ follow-ups), referrals / escalations, innovation pool, comments + mentions, alerts, vehicle plan (seed today's equipment from backend `vehicle_feature` once an endpoint exists), quality check (`ai/quality.ts` on mapped requirements), deck (`requirementDeck` on mapped data), search (combine backend board `q` and sidecar). Persist the sidecar later as backend tables (option 2).
411	
412	**Step 5 — Verify.**
413	- `npm run contract-test` with `API_BASE=http://localhost:3000/api` and `DATA_SOURCE=backend` (parametrize the IDs: pick the first open case and a confirmed one from the board instead of `CASE-G60-0001`).
414	- Backend: `uv run pytest` and `uv run python -m app.demo e2e "G60 / USA"`.
415	- Click through the demo storyline with real data; check the audit trail shows backend events (actor `pm:<uuid>`).
416	
417	### 8.5 Decisions the team must make
418	
419	1. **Which data source per screen for the demo** (real where it exists, sidecar for the rest, or full mock as fallback)? Recommendation: real for signals, cases, scores, requirements, chat, audit; sidecar for collaboration.
420	2. **Persona ↔ backend user ↔ config mapping** (8.4 step 1). Do we keep the six named personas on real data?
421	3. **Requirement statuses:** extend the backend flow with `signed_off` (head) and `planned`/`exported`, or keep them as a frontend layer? Recommendation: extend the backend (two statuses + who may set them), small change in `requirements/service.py` and the check constraint.
422	4. **Structured requirement editing:** add `PATCH /requirements/{id}` for metrics, acceptance criteria, assumptions, scope (audited like the rest), or keep editing the page markdown only?
423	5. **Brand fit:** factor (frontend) or multiplier (backend)? Recommendation: follow the backend (multiplier); the weights panel hides the `brand_fit` slider and shows the brand-fit tag instead; add `reach` as a slider.
424	6. **Case workflow:** do the frontend sub-states (investigating, awaiting answers, ready) and outcomes (refer, innovation pool, park) become backend concepts? Recommendation: store them in the sidecar first; later a `case_vehicle.workflow` column + `referral` and `innovation` tables.
425	7. **Chat:** backend RAG agent for free-form questions (OpenAI key needed), keep the scripted flows (draft requirement, questions for engineering, segment mode) in the adapter?
426	8. **Which ID the UI shows for signals:** uuid, or the readable `record_id` (`bmw_feedback-G60-0001`, matching the old `G60-0001` style)?
427	
428	---
429	
430	## 9. Gotchas
431	
432	- **Scale.** The mock has 28 cases and ~500 signals; the backend has 1,206 cases (376 opened by rule per line pair), ~13,000 valid signals. The case board should show `open` + `confirmed` by default (backend default) and the Sankey needs aggregated counts (sources × car areas × cases) rather than every signal: add an aggregate endpoint or compute from `GET /cases?profile_id` (per-case `source_types`, `markets`, `distinct_customers`).
433	- **"Invalidate everything after a mutation"** (`hooks.ts`) re-fetches all active queries; with real data, narrow it to the affected keys if screens get slow.
434	- **Stale saves:** backend returns 409 when `expected_version` is old; the UI must reload the page instead of overwriting.
435	- **Per-vehicle actions:** every case action on the backend needs the vehicle (`/vehicles/{vehicle}/…`). Use the persona's config vehicle; Baukasten cases appear for several lines and each line decides separately.
436	- **Permissions differ:** backend lets any PM of one of the case's lines act; the frontend uses owner/co-owners. Until owners exist in the backend, check ownership in the adapter (sidecar) before calling.
437	- **Market labels:** `Rest of World` has spaces; URL-encode it in query strings.
438	- **Citations:** the UI's markdown turns `[ID]` into clickable links that open the signal on the case page. Backend signal ids are uuids, and the case page must be able to find them (the signals of the case must be loaded with the same ids).
439	- **Real data has no Chinese verbatims** for G60/G70 feedback (US-heavy). The UI says so honestly; keep that (segment chips show `China (0)`).
440	- **LLM keys:** backend needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` for the RAG agent's LLM mode and the classifier (2,557 signals still unclassified); without it the agent answers extractively with citations. The frontend's optional live features use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
441	- **`docs/` vs `All-context/`:** the frontend branch still has `docs/` (seed script reads `docs/02-data/processed`); `main` uses `All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/processed`. Point `web/scripts/seed.ts` at `All-context` when `docs/` is removed.
442	- **Synthetic labels:** real backend objects are not synthetic; personas, sidecar content and demo decisions are. Keep the `synthetic` flag honest in the mapping.
443	
444	---
445	
446	## 10. Quick reference: where to look
447	
448	| Need | File |
449	|---|---|
450	| Frontend endpoint list and schemas | `web/src/contracts/api.ts`, `entities.ts`, `enums.ts` (or `contracts/openapi.yaml`) |
451	| Frontend business rules | `web/src/mock/handlers.ts`, `web/src/mock/scoring.ts`, `web/src/mock/ai/*` |
452	| Where the data source is chosen | `web/src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts`, `web/src/lib/api/client.ts` |
453	| Demo storyline and personas | `web/README.md`, `web/src/mock/authored/*` |
454	| Backend API guide | `backend/API.md`, `backend/app/api/routers/*.py`, `http://localhost:8000/docs` |
455	| Backend data model and rules | `database-design.md`, `data-model.mmd`, `CLAUDE.md` |
456	| Backend decisions and progress | `plan.md`, `changes.md` |
457	| Taxonomy | `taxonomy/README.md`, `taxonomy/taxonomy.json` |
458	| Meeting feedback that shaped the UI | `All-context/03-meetings-with-pm/` (Thomas demo feedback, PM interviews) |

# Integration guide: frontend (`web/`) ↔ backend (`backend/`)

**For:** whoever (human or AI agent) connects the synthetic-data frontend to Ghassen's real backend.
**State as of 11.10.2026, 02:30:** frontend on branch `feature/frontend-demo` ([PR #5](https://github.com/ghassenzaara/BMW-Product-Management-Challenge/pull/5) into `main`); backend on `main` (phases 0 to 10 done, see `plan.md`).

> **How to use this file.** Read sections 1 to 3 to understand the product and the two codebases, then section 7 (the gap) and section 8 (the plan). Sections 4 to 6 are reference material: every screen, endpoint and business rule of the frontend, so nothing gets lost while swapping the data source.

---

## 0. TL;DR

- The **frontend** is a Next.js 16 app that talks to **its own REST contract** (`web/src/contracts/*.ts`, Zod, exported to `contracts/openapi.yaml`). Today that contract is served by a **mock backend inside Next.js** (`web/src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts` + `web/src/mock/`) on synthetic data plus 404 real BMW verbatims.
- The **backend** is FastAPI + Postgres/pgvector (Supabase) with **its own, different REST API** (`backend/app/api/routers/*.py`, guide in `backend/API.md`), on the full real data (1,206 cases, ~13,000 signals, scores for 10 configs, RAG index).
- The two APIs **do not match** (different paths, field names, vocabularies, IDs and concepts: per-vehicle case state, configs and weight profiles per vehicle × market, page-based requirements). About half of the UI features (open questions, meeting notes, referrals, innovation pool, vehicle plan, comments, alerts, head sign-off, quality check, segments, deck) **have no backend counterpart yet**.
- **Recommended approach: an adapter layer (BFF) inside Next.js.** Keep the UI and its contract unchanged; replace the mock handlers endpoint by endpoint with handlers that call FastAPI and map the shapes. Features the backend lacks keep running on a small "sidecar" store keyed by real IDs. Switchable per endpoint, so the demo can always fall back to the mock. Details and step-by-step plan in section 8.

---

## 1. The product in one page

BMW product managers (PMs) decide which customer requirements go into the next generation of a vehicle (G60 = 5 Series, F70 = 1 Series, G70 = 7 Series). The app turns heterogeneous evidence into traceable, prioritized requirements, with the PM deciding at every step.

**Chain:** `Signal → Case → Requirement → Vehicle plan → Codebeamer`

| Concept | Meaning | Frontend entity | Backend table |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Signal** | One piece of evidence with its source: a BMW verbatim, a study row, a web review, a competitor fact | `Signal` | `signal` (+ `source_record`) |
| **Case** | A customer **problem**, built from a group of signals on one topic. Has an importance score, **no cost** | `Case` | `case_item` + `case_vehicle` (per line) + `case_score` |
| **Requirement** | What BMW builds to solve a confirmed case: SMART text, measurable targets, release, rough cost | `Requirement` | `requirement` |
| **Vehicle plan** | Requirements of a series grouped by car area, next to today's equipment; exported to Codebeamer | `VehiclePlan` / `PlannedFeature` | (none; `vehicle_feature` holds today's equipment) |

**Non-negotiable rules (both codebases agree):**
1. **AI proposes, PM decides.** The AI never edits directly: it returns proposals (frontend `Proposal`, backend `chat_message.proposed_diff`) that a person accepts or rejects.
2. **Every human decision has a reason** and every change writes an **append-only audit event** (who or what, when, before/after, rationale).
3. **Traceability:** every requirement links back to its case, the case to its signals, signals to their source quote.
4. **Fixed taxonomy:** 11 car areas, 219 topics, 11 aspect groups (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`). Agents classify into it; they never invent categories (Thomas's feedback).
5. **Customer-facing requirements only:** regulatory, engineering specs and pricing are out of scope.
6. **Score formula is explainable:** case score = weighted mean of factors (0..1); requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier (S/M/L).

**Personas (frontend demo, synthetic):** Lena Hofmann (PM 5 Series, rest of world), Wei Zhang (PM 5 Series, China), Jonas Berger (cross-series attribute PM, operating concept / HMI, "Baukasten"), Katrin Maier (head of product line: signs off, resolves escalations), Sofia Rossi (PM 1 Series), Daniel Okafor (PM 7 Series).

---

## 2. Repository map

```

## 3. How the frontend works (architecture)

### 3.1 Contract-first
- Every endpoint is declared once in `web/src/contracts/api.ts` (`endpoints` object: method, path, query, body, response as Zod schemas). Entities in `entities.ts`, vocabularies in `enums.ts`, UI labels in `labels.ts`.
- `npm run export-contract` writes `contracts/openapi.yaml` and `contracts/schemas/*.json`.
- `npm run contract-test` (`API_BASE=…`) calls every endpoint against a running server, validates every response with Zod, and walks the demo storyline. **Any data source behind the UI must pass it** (the storyline uses seeded IDs such as `CASE-G60-0001`, so it needs parametrizing for real data).

### 3.2 Data access
- The UI never imports `src/mock`. It calls `api(name, { params, query, body })` from `src/lib/api/client.ts`, or the hooks `useApi(name, opts)` / `useApiMutation(name)` from `src/lib/api/hooks.ts`.
- Base URL: `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` (default `/api` = the mock route).
- **Every successful mutation invalidates every query** (`qc.invalidateQueries()`): simple and always consistent, fine for demo-sized data. With 13,000 real signals some screens will need pagination (section 9).
- Errors: the client expects `{ error: string, issues? }` and an HTTP status; it throws `ApiRequestError`, shown as a toast.

### 3.3 Auth (demo)
- `/login` lists users (`GET /users`); picking one sets the cookie `rs_user` (`src/lib/session.ts`). The client sends it as header `x-user-id`. The mock route resolves the user from its store (`u-lena`, `u-wei`, `u-jonas`, `u-katrin`, `u-sofia`, `u-daniel`).

### 3.4 The mock backend
- `route.ts` matches method + path against the contract, parses query/body with Zod, calls `handlers[name]({ params, query, body, user })`, validates the response in dev, maps `ApiError(status)` to JSON errors.
- `src/mock/store.ts`: one in-memory `Dataset` (shape = `Dataset` entity) cloned from `fixtures/seed.json`; `audit()`, `notify()`, `nextId()`, `now()`; `POST /admin/reset` restores the seed. Quality checks live in a side map (`checks()`).
- `src/mock/handlers.ts`: one function per endpoint, holding the business rules (section 6).
- `src/mock/scoring.ts`: reference scorer. `src/mock/ai/*`: scripted AI (chat intents, drafts, meeting-note extraction, quality check, segments); `ai/live.ts` optionally calls Claude when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set (free-form chat, quality-check LLM pass, segment summary). The backend uses OpenAI; after integration the chat should go to the backend RAG agent.
- Seed: `npm run seed` rebuilds `seed.json` from the real CSVs in `docs/02-data/processed/` (404 selected verbatims, study rows, 2030 sales) plus authored synthetic content (people, web signals, competitor facts, decisions, requirements, audit history). Synthetic objects carry `synthetic: true` and the UI tags them.

### 3.5 Running it
```bash
cd web
npm install
npm run dev          # http://localhost:3000, pick a persona
npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build
API_BASE=http://localhost:3000/api npm run contract-test
```

## 6. Business logic implemented in the frontend mock

These rules live in `web/src/mock/handlers.ts` and `web/src/mock/ai/*`. Whatever replaces the mock must keep them (in the backend, the adapter or the sidecar).

### 6.1 Permissions
- Only the case **owner or a co-owner** (or the head) changes a case; everyone can read, comment, watch, escalate. Only the requirement owner (or head) edits it.
- **Head of product line** (`role = head`) sends back, signs off, resolves escalations, edits the brand profile and default weight profiles.
- Series PMs (plan `ownerIds`) edit the vehicle plan.

### 6.2 Case lifecycle (frontend)
- States: `observed → new → investigating → awaiting_answers → ready → decided`. Actions `open`, `start`, `await`, `ready`, `reopen` move the state; every move needs a rationale.
- Deciding sets `state = decided` and an **outcome**: `confirm` (drafts requirements via the requirement agent if none exist), `refer` (to another PM: creates a `Referral`, the receiver becomes a watcher and is notified), `innovation` (adds to the pool with a horizon and the PM's pitch), `park`, `reject`, `merge` (moves signals into the target, recomputes its figures, notifies the target owner).
- `refer` with `escalate: true` creates an **escalation** to the head instead (anyone involved may escalate, e.g. China vs. rest-of-world conflict).
- Every decision is prepended to the case page's "Decision log" and audited.
- Referral decisions: `accept` creates a **linked case** in the receiver's workspace (`originCaseId`), `decline` puts the source case back to `ready`, `escalate` hands it to the head, `resolve` (head) records a resolution (one market, market variant, keep both, take over, return) in the case context and decision log.

### 6.3 Requirement lifecycle (frontend)
`draft → in_discussion → pm_approved → signed_off → planned → exported`, plus `rejected` (restore → `draft`).
- `approve` (owner, from draft or in discussion) notifies the head with a sign-off request; the open quality-check issues are recorded in the audit event (section 6.9).
- `send_back` (head, from pm_approved) → `in_discussion` with `sentBackReason`, owner notified.
- `sign_off` (head, from pm_approved) → owner notified.
- `plan` (owner/head, from signed_off) links or creates a `PlannedFeature` in the series plan.
- `export` (from planned); the Codebeamer export also moves every planned requirement to `exported`.
- IDs: `REQ-<series>-NNNN`, China variants `REQ-<series>-CN-NNNN`.

### 6.4 Scoring (reference, `mock/scoring.ts`)
- Factors (all 0..1): `customers`, `severity`, `satisfaction_gap`, `competitor_gap`, `market_volume`, `regression`, `trend`, `brand_fit`.
- `case score = Σ w_f · factor_f / Σ w_f` (no cost). `requirement score = case score × costMultiplier[size]`.
- Manual ranks (with reason) win over the computed order. Observed, rejected and merged cases are not ranked.
- `previewScores` re-ranks with unsaved weights; the UI shows "moved because…" and a robustness column (stays in the top 5 under every profile).
- `customers` is recomputed from the case's signals: `log10(1 + n) / log10(61)`.

### 6.5 AI assistant (`mock/ai/chat.ts`, scripted unless a key is set)
Intent by message text; every answer cites evidence as `[SIGNAL-ID]`, and every change is a proposal:
- "research …" → mock research run adds two synthetic web signals to the case (audited as `agent:researcher`).
- "draft a SMART requirement" → `new_requirement` proposal(s) from `ai/drafts.ts`.
- "what should I ask engineering/finance" → `new_question` proposals.
- "why is this ranked so high", "compare the markets", "what do competitors offer", "argument sheet", "set the target to …" (field proposal) → cited answers.
- Free-form questions go to the live LLM when available (context: case, figures, up to 40 signals, page, requirement).
- `savePmContext` stores the PM's market focus, cost sensitivity, positioning, timing and note in the case context, then the assistant posts 1 to 2 follow-up questions the data cannot answer (market mismatch, platform change vs. LCI, paid option vs. standard, match/beat competitors).
- `addMeetingNote` (`ai/notes.ts`) extracts answers to open questions, field updates and decision-log entries from pasted notes as proposals.
- Proposal kinds: `field`, `body`, `question_answer`, `new_question`, `new_requirement`. Accepting applies the change, logs a context entry and an audit event.

### 6.6 Monitoring and refresh
- `refresh` runs once over a pool of authored web findings: new signals attach to their case, owners and watchers are notified, a competitor fact with a metric raises an **alert** ("raises the bar") on the case; a second run finds nothing (dedupe by URL and content hash). An `AgentRun` is recorded.
- `resolveAlert`: dismiss, or `rework` (requirement back to in_discussion, case back to investigating).

### 6.7 Vehicle plan and export
- The plan lists features per car area with today's availability (standard/optional/absent/removed), action (keep/new/improve/remove), release, protected flag and linked requirements.
- Codebeamer CSV columns: ID, Summary, Description, Category, Market, Release, Priority, Score, Evidence level, Metrics, Acceptance criteria, Assumptions, Cost size, Cost band, Linked case, Linked findings, Rationale, Status. Sorted by rank under the user's weight profile.

### 6.8 Engineering deck (`requirementDeck` + `web/src/lib/deck.ts`)
Signed-off, planned and exported requirements of a series, sorted by rank. Per slide: SMART text and metrics, top 3 BMW complaint quotes (not likes), score breakdown (factor value × normalized weight), competitor gap, last 5 decisions (requirement and case), open quality issues. Rendered client-side with `pptxgenjs`. Easy to rebuild on real data: it only needs requirement, case factors + weights, case signals and decisions.

### 6.9 Quality check (`mock/ai/quality.ts`)
Runs automatically after drafting and every edit, and on demand. Warns, never blocks; approving lists the open issues and requires a reason.
- `vague_word` (title, description, acceptance criteria: "improved", "better", "user-friendly", "intuitive", "seamless", …; red if no metric has a numeric target).
- `missing_scope` (scope global while > 80 % of the case's verbatims come from one market; China scope with < 3 Chinese verbatims).
- `out_of_scope` (homologation, type approval, UN-R, ISO 26262, emissions, crash test, ECU, CAN bus, supplier, part number, price/pricing, business case) — red.
- `duplicate` (≥ 30 % word overlap with a live requirement of the same series, red) / `baukasten` (same in another series, or the case spans several series, amber, suggests the cross-series PM).
- `conflict` (same metric question with another target in the same car area; or relies on a feature the plan removes).
- Optional LLM pass adds issues of the same kinds (strict JSON, related IDs validated).
Portable as-is: inputs are a requirement, its case figures, all requirements and the plan. Could later move to Python next to `requirements/service.py`.

### 6.10 Ask the segment (`mock/ai/segment.ts`)
- Segments = markets of the case (+ market × powertrain with ≥ 3 verbatims), counted **only from real BMW verbatims** (no synthetic, no web).
- With verbatims: counts by kind + 3 to 5 strongest quotes, cited. Live LLM gets only that segment's quotes and must summarize in the third person; citations not in the set are dropped.
- Without verbatims: "No evidence for China owners", the closest segment with data, and a `new_question` proposal to the market PM. Never a guess.
- On real data: segments come from `GET /signals?case_id=…` filtered by `evidence_role = bmw_customer` (or `source_id = bmw_feedback`), grouped by `market` and `powertrain`.

### 6.11 Audit actions written by the mock
`case.created/edited/state_changed/decided/pm_context_saved/exported_md`, `requirement.drafted/edited/status_changed/checked/deck_exported`, `requirements.exported`, `proposal.accepted/rejected/created`, `question.created/answered/edited`, `meeting_note.added`, `referral.*`, `escalation.*`, `alert.*`, `plan.feature_*`, `signals.fetched/researched`, `segment.asked`, `comment.added`, `weight_profile.*`, `brand_profile.updated`, `workspace.updated`. Actor = user id or `agent:<name>`.
